newsitem.title: CANADA: Canola, flax prices seen up 10-20 pct - Ag Canada.
newsitem.headline: Canola, flax prices seen up 10-20 pct - Ag Canada.

text.p: Canadian canola and flax prices were forecast on Thursday to be 10 to 20 percent higher in crop year 1996/97 (Aug/July) compared with the previous year, Agriculture Canada said in its October economic analysis.
Reduced output and higher demand were seen raising prices.

Canola production was forecast at 4.98 million tonnes this fall compared with 6.44 million tonnes last year. Prices were seen ranging from C$460 to C$500 a tonne in 1996/97, up from the average C$432 the previous year.
"This, combined with strong export demand, and a major expansion in domestic crush, is expected to cause canola prices to average about 10 percent higher," Ag Canada said.

Flax output was expected to be 859,000 tonnes this fall compared to the previous harvest at 1.105 million tonnes. Flax prices were forecast between C$385 to C$425 a tonne in 1996/97, up from the average C$341 the previous year.
"The 1996/97 average Canadian flaxseed price is expected to increase by about 20 percent," Ag Canada said.
